text: Sample context: CIL wants an enterprise architecture that supports growth to 2030 across nutrients, crop protection and retail, absorbs NACL, and puts farmer and dealer data to work. The CIO's priorities are a clean SAP core on RISE, cloud-smart hosting on Azure, one governed integration and data layer, AI that is grounded in trusted data, and security that covers plants and the retail edge.

docs.text:
# CIO Strategy Brief (sample)

## Business context
Coromandel International is a Murugappa Group company in farm inputs: phosphatic fertilisers, specialty nutrients, crop protection, organic products and a retail network of Gromor stores. Growth to 2030 rests on five moves: expand crop protection and specialty nutrients, scale Nano fertilisers, grow the retail and dealer channel, build agri-tech services such as drone spraying, and integrate the acquired NACL Industries business.

## What the business expects from IT
- One view of the farmer, dealer and retailer across apps, stores and field teams.
- Faster, rule-based decisions on dealer credit, schemes and pricing.
- Season-aware demand and supply planning across plants, depots and stores.
- Subsidy claims reconciled without spreadsheets.
- Plant reliability and safety improved through data from the historian and labs.

## Technology direction
- Keep the SAP S/4HANA core clean on RISE; extend on BTP rather than custom code in the core.
- Cloud-smart on Microsoft Azure; keep on-premise only what must stay near the plants.
- A governed API and event layer instead of new point-to-point links.
- An enterprise data platform with owned, classified data domains, so AI use cases run on trusted data.
- Generative and predictive AI for agronomy advice, forecasting and service desks, with responsible-AI controls.
- Zero-trust security across IT, OT and the retail edge; DPDP Act 2023 compliance for farmer and employee data.

## Constraints
Multi-site plants with OT that must stay segregated, a large field and retail workforce on mobile devices, partner platforms for satellite advisory and drones, and limited in-house architecture capacity.

docs.text:
# Workshop notes: Sales, Retail and Farmer Services (sample)

Participants: regional sales heads, retail operations, farmer services, IT business partners.

## Pain points raised
1. Dealer credit limits and scheme eligibility are worked out in spreadsheets and email before SAP is updated.
2. Two farmer apps (MyGromor and Nutri Connect) and a WhatsApp bot give overlapping advice; farmers register more than once.
3. Store POS does not post sales to SAP in real time; stock at Gromor stores is reconciled weekly.
4. Soil test results from Nutri clinics do not reach the farmer app or the agronomists' recommendations.
5. Demand for kharif and rabi is forecast in Excel by each region; plants plan on last year's numbers.
6. Subsidy claims are reconciled against iFMS manually each month.

## Expectations
- A single farmer and dealer record shared by apps, stores and the sales team.
- Advisory that combines soil tests, satellite and drone imagery, weather and purchase history.
- Field teams on one mobile app with offline support.
- Dashboards for sell-through, stock and scheme performance by district.

docs.name: Sample - IT Landscape Summary.txt
docs.text:
IT LANDSCAPE SUMMARY (sample)

Hosting: primary data centre in Hyderabad, DR site in Chennai, Microsoft Azure for new workloads, SAP S/4HANA on RISE (SAP-managed), SaaS for Microsoft 365, SuccessFactors and Power BI. Hosting for several field and retail apps is not documented.

Integration: most interfaces are point-to-point or file transfers; an API gateway exists but few interfaces use it. No event broker.

Data: reports are built in Power BI on extracts from source systems. No enterprise data catalogue, master data for dealers and farmers is duplicated across apps, personal data is not consistently classified.

Security and resilience: SSO through Entra ID for most corporate apps but not all subsidiaries; backups are VM and storage snapshots; RPO and RTO are not defined per tier; security monitoring of the OT/IT boundary and retail stores is unconfirmed.

AI: predictive maintenance and a retail retention model run as pilots on Azure; there is no MLOps pipeline. Microsoft 365 Copilot is licensed for a pilot group.

Operational technology: DCS, SCADA and PLCs at the plants, AVEVA PI historian, lab systems for quality control. OT is outside the detailed scope of this assessment.
